- Removal-type changes save a little more than the MAC model predicts, so I keep a −2% bias on them.

**Exchange rates (s saved per pp lost).**
- Epoch dial: about 1–2.5.
- Stem freeze at 75%: about 2. At 71% (E055): −0.17 pp seeds 0–2 for 0.07 s, worse than the dial. At 60%: a cliff.
- Group-2 freeze at 90%: close to free. At 85%: no better than the dial.

**Funders.** Every booster tried has read ≤0. My prior for a new one is −0.05 ± 0.2 pp. Accuracy is bought with steps.

That makes ||ΔW||/||W|| track the LR schedule almost exactly, not learning progress. Update-rate curves for the filter groups will just redraw the schedules I imposed. They can't predict freeze cost. Only gradient-norm or loss-sensitivity probes could do that, and even those are confounded by the resolution switches.

**Mechanisms.**
1. Lookahead is worth about 1 pp and is near its optimum.
2. The late 28/32 px phases carry accuracy.
3. Early accuracy is carried by steps and the LR schedule, not by pixels.
4. The free part of backward truncation is used up, except perhaps the whitening detach moving earlier, which is worth ≤0.07 s.
5. Filter wd is inert because Muon renormalizes the filters.

7. The harness passes fine labels only. Using coarse labels probably needs a table from outside the provided data, so it is probably blocked.

**Strategy.** The remaining value lies in the gate and accounting (I088/I089/I090), not in new levers.

- The size of σ_build.
- Winner's curse vs seed-set difficulty (H4.4).

W3 (cost lens), after E055.

**Tip (E049, 3df6233).** E036 plus a group-2 freeze (annealed from 75%, frozen for the last 10%) plus 0.25 epoch: 237 steps at batch 2000.
- Resolution: 20/24/28/32 px at 30/10/30/30%. Whitening detached at 20%, stem frozen at 75%.
- Builds read 0.7535 / 5.198 s and 0.7552 / 5.206 s.
- Population mean is about 0.7535–0.754. Against the 0.75 bar that leaves only about 0.3 pp of margin after allowing for judge drift and rebuild drift.

**Noise.**
- Rebuilding identical math moves the 3-seed mean by about ±0.25 pp. Per-seed SD is about 0.3 pp.
- Time reproduces to about 1%.
- A same-build comparison over 20 seeds resolves about 0.1 pp. Rebuild SD probably adds 0.05–0.15 pp per 20-seed mean (E036's 3-seed reads ran 0.7497–0.7544).
- Seeds 0–2 can't see effects under 0.2 pp.

**Time model.** Time ≈ 0.25 s + Σ(steps × per-step cost).
- Per-step cost: 32 px 0.032 s, 28 px 0.026 s, 24 px 0.021 s, 20 px 0.016 s.
- The stem freeze saves about 0.0087 s per step at 32 px. The group-2 freeze saves about 0.010 s more.
- E055 (stem freeze 75%→71%, about 10 more frozen steps) saved only about 0.07 s, about 0.007 s per step. That fits.
- Removal-type changes save a little more than the MAC model predicts, so I keep a −2% bias on them.

**Exchange rates (s saved per pp lost).**
- Epoch dial: about 1–2.5.
- Stem freeze at 75%: about 2. At 71% (E055): −0.17 pp seeds 0–2 for 0.07 s, worse than the dial. At 60%: a cliff.
- Group-2 freeze at 90%: close to free. At 85%: no better than the dial.
- Intermittent stem: about 0.7–1. Width: about 0.7. Stride instead of pool: about 0.45.

**Stem mechanism.** The stem keeps adapting until about 75%, and that includes the 28→32 switch. E037, E042, E054 and E055 all say that cutting its updates earlier costs more than the dial. The 75% point looks close to optimal, and doses near it are convex.

**Funders.** Every booster tried has read ≤0. My prior for a new one is −0.05 ± 0.2 pp. Accuracy is bought with steps.

**Key structural point for H7.** Under Muon the weights are renormalized to a fixed norm and the update is orthogonalized, so its norm is roughly fixed. That makes ||ΔW||/||W|| track the LR schedule almost exactly, not learning progress. Update-rate curves for the filter groups will just redraw the schedules I imposed. They can't predict freeze cost. Only gradient-norm or loss-sensitivity probes could do that, and even those are confounded by the resolution switches.

**Mechanisms.**
1. Lookahead is worth about 1 pp and is near its optimum.
2. The late 28/32 px phases carry accuracy.
3. Early accuracy is carried by steps and the LR schedule, not by pixels.
4. The free part of backward truncation is used up, except perhaps the whitening detach moving earlier, which is worth ≤0.07 s.
5. Filter wd is inert because Muon renormalizes the filters.
6. BN scale is already frozen in the code (`requires_grad=False`), so H1.5.10 closes from the code alone.
7. The harness passes fine labels only. Using coarse labels probably needs a table from outside the provided data, so it is probably blocked.

**Strategy.** The remaining value lies in the gate and accounting (I088/I089/I090), not in new levers.
- If σ_build is about 0.1 pp, the gate needs a population mean of about 0.7523. That rules out E052 and E053 (~0.7515–0.752), and possibly E046 too.
- A tighter honest gate may then prove E049 itself is barely safe. In that case spending steps, not cutting them, becomes rational.

**Unsure.**
- The size of σ_build.
- Winner's curse vs seed-set difficulty (H4.4).
- Whether E052 or E053 clear 0.7523 on fresh seeds. I lean no.

forecasts.reason: Diagnostic that re-runs the tip. E036's spread of 3-seed means across builds (0.7497–0.7544) points to a correlated build component ≥0.08 pp.
E052/E053 sat about 0.2 pp below E049 on seeds 13–32, so about 0.7515–0.752. With σ_build around 0.1, the gate needs ≥0.7523, so both probably fail P≥0.9.
A 0.25-epoch dial step is worth about 0.1 pp. That is comparable to σ_build plus the SE, so the interval will straddle the predicted 0.06–0.18 band.
TrainingData exposes fine labels only, so it is likely blocked. Even if it runs, my booster prior is −0.05±0.2 pp.
BatchNorm.__init__ already sets weight.requires_grad=False, so there is no time to save. Closed by reading the code.
About 33 extra detached 20/24 px steps at about 1.5–2 ms each saves about 0.06 s (≈1%), the low end of the predicted range. The accuracy cost is probably ≤0.1 pp but can't be resolved.
With Muon renormalization and an orthogonalized update, ||ΔW||/||W|| just follows the imposed LR schedules. The curves therefore can't separate E028 from E037/E055 independently.

cruxes: What is σ_build for a 20-seed mean? If it is ≥0.1 pp, the honest gate needs a population mean of about 0.7523+. That excludes E052/E053/E046, and E049 itself becomes marginal, so the loop should spend steps for margin instead of cutting time.
Is the ~0.2 pp post-keep challenger deficit winner's curse (H4.4.3)? If so, the fresh-seed gaps of E052/E053 to E049 shrink, and a ~0.1 s cheaper recipe may pass.
Under Muon's fixed-norm weights, does any per-group learning-progress signal (gradient norm, not ||ΔW||/||W||) predict freeze cost? If not, H7 cannot replace dose sweeps.
